params.body:
Measured first. A run costs **eleven billed minutes**:

| job | min/run |
|---|---|
| phpunit | 5,1 |
| Static analysis | 1,9 |
| the five small ones | 1 each |

The five small ones cost five minutes for about two minutes of work, because GitHub rounds every
job up to a whole minute. At about thirty-two runs a day this week that is some seven thousand
minutes a month against three thousand included, and every minute above that is billed.

**Two changes, and not one test fewer.**

**A superseded run is cancelled.** Push twice to the same branch and the first run is about code
that no longer exists. On pull requests only: every commit on main stays measured, because the
coverage report Elixir reads and the build Forge deploys both hang on it. The concurrency group
carries the event, so a pull request run can never cancel the main run of the commit it was merged
into.

**The four quality jobs run on the pull request and not again on main.** `up-to-date` already says
a pull request was built on the current main, so repeating them on main measures the same code
twice.

What that gives up, named plainly: the one case where it is *not* the same code — two pull requests
merged in quick succession, the second one current when it ran and no longer when it landed. That
happened yesterday (671 went in while it was behind 668). The answer is to re-propose a pull request
whose `up-to-date` is red, which costs me a minute, rather than to buy four checks twice on every
merge forever. phpunit and assets do stay on main: the first because Elixir reads its report from
there, the second because main is what Forge deploys and a red build here is a failed deploy there.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| pull request | 11 min | 11 min |
| main after the merge | 11 min | 6 min |
| a superseded push | runs out | cancelled |

Twenty-two billed minutes per change becomes seventeen. If the pace stays this high, the next step
is a runner of our own on a small VM (about five euro a month, minutes free), and that one is worth
its own conversation rather than a pull request.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
params.title: A run costs eleven billed minutes, and every change was paying twice
